intro.author: Traditionally Moses, who is said to have written down Israel's journey stages (33:2). Many scholars think the book was compiled from several sources over time.
intro.written: Traditionally near the end of the wilderness years, on the plains of Moab; many scholars date its final form later.
intro.audience: The new generation of Israel, about to enter the promised land, learning from their parents' failures
intro.setting: The book covers nearly forty years, from Israel's departure from Mount Sinai to its camp on the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho. The English name comes from its two censuses; the Hebrew title means 'In the wilderness.'
intro.purpose: To show how God kept leading and providing for his people through their complaints and rebellions, and kept his promise to bring a new generation to the edge of the land.
intro.bigIdea: God stays faithful through the wilderness, even when his people do not.

outline.title: Balaam and the sin at Peor
